newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's forward book improves in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's forward book improves in first quarter.

text.p: South African government debt related to the forward cover book operated on its behalf by the Reserve Bank showed a marked reduction in the first quarter of 1997, figures released by the finance ministry on Friday showed.
The deficit on the Gold and Foreign Exchange Contingency Reserve Account had been provisionally projected at 3.65 billion rand at the end of the 1996/97 fiscal year on March 31.
In fact, due in part to profits realised on the provision of forward cover by the central bank in the first three months of 1997, the deficit came in at 2.17 billion.
A stock issue to the Reserve Bank to redeem this liability was not currently envisaged, the ministry added.
The scale of the Reserve Bank's forward cover position has been a matter of persistent concern to the foreign exchange markets.

However, economists say the relative stability of the rand so far this year has reduced demand for forward cover among South African corporates, allowing the central bank to unwind some of its oversold positions.
